title: The Formation of Black Holes and Singularities in Spherically Symmetric Gravitational Collapse
relevance: Primary source for the coupled Einstein–massless-scalar collapse theorem, zero-mass flatness criterion, and characteristic estimates audited in this lane; it supports the conditional forward-cone flat-centre corollary but does not prove the desired finite incoming-coordinate causal barrier.
limits: Bounded selected audit only: main-text prose extracted throughout; §§2–4, Proposition 4.1, Theorem 5.1(a)–(j), selected proof pages and Figure 1 checked at the locators below. Cited prior existence/global-structure proofs were not audited; the remaining radial constraints were not solved independently; no maximal globally hyperbolic or complete-past extension, entire-past matching, or common-future separation is established.

assumptions: Spherically symmetric Einstein–massless-minimally-coupled-real-scalar system; regular timelike centre; initial future null cone with stated affine normalization, asymptotic completeness and bounded initial Bondi mass as introduced in §4; theorem's annular concentration inequality. Paper restricts its spacetime to the future of the initial cone (p.356).
conclusion: Theorem 5.1 supplies marginal-sphere, event-horizon, trapped-cone, singular-boundary and quantitative proper-time/area-radius conclusions. With zero scalar data inside the annulus, the theorem's bounds conditionally place a regular flat central event beyond the horizon vertex and before the inner incoming boundary arrives. The audited source does not provide a finite global incoming-coordinate causal barrier proving a selected exterior event has no common future with that centre event.
